fields.features_heading: What Emergent Builds for Each Training Stage
fields.features_subheading: Tell Emergent which program the survey follows and who acts on it. It builds the survey, the dashboard, and the table behind them.
fields.feature_1:
Questions for each stage of a program

Name the program and the stage it has reached. Emergent drafts skill ratings for before it starts, a knowledge check for the day after, and a behavior question for 90 days on.
fields.feature_2:
Answers tagged by team and program

Each answer is saved as a row in a database you own, with the team, program, and survey date on it. Put this year's skill ratings beside last year's before the budget meeting.
fields.feature_3:
Learner and manager answers side by side

A learner's answer sits beside their manager's answer to the same question. The dashboard shows where the two agree and lists every pair that does not, sorted by program and team.
fields.feature_4:
One question per screen on a phone

Supervisors on a warehouse floor answer one question per screen on a phone, between shifts. No response cap applies, whether a pilot group of 12 answers or all 1,400 staff do.
fields.feature_5:
Linked to your HR system

Connect the survey to your HR system or any tool with an API. The app pulls each person's department and manager from it, and no one has to type them into the survey by hand.
fields.feature_6:
Your domain, and your code on GitHub

Your own domain hosts the survey: custom domains are included and use credits. On paid plans, Emergent exports the full code to your GitHub repository, ready to extend or self-host.

fields.usecase_heading: What Four Training Teams Acted On
fields.tab_content_1:
In a 4-skill check, coaching rates 2.6

Thornfield Freight sets its training plan each December, after its 48 shift supervisors rate their confidence in 4 skills from 1 to 5. This year 44 answered. Safety rules led at 4.3. Coaching came last at 2.6, behind handling conflict at 3.1. The first workshop of the new year is on coaching.
fields.tab_content_2:
On the knowledge check, 15 reps miss walk-away pricing

Tregarth Software ran 2 days of negotiation training for 36 account managers, then sent a relevance rating and a 5-question knowledge check. Of the 36, 34 answered, and relevance averaged 4.4. On the walk-away price question, 15 of the 34 got it wrong. The trainer built a role play on it.
fields.tab_content_3:
Directors confirm only 13 weekly one-on-ones

Vinterly Home Care trained 22 new nurse managers. At day 90, each graduate and their director answered one question: does this manager hold a weekly one-on-one with every direct report? Twenty graduates said yes. Directors confirmed 13. The training lead got a Slack message naming the 7 pairs that disagreed.
fields.tab_content_4:
Thirty-eight employees want SQL, and a cohort starts

Osterbrook Analytics asks all 120 employees each January which skill they want to grow and how they learn best. This year 96 answered, and 38 picked SQL. Of the 96, 52 said they learn best from a colleague. The first cohort is an 8-week SQL group led by peer mentors.

fields.howto_title: How to Write Learning Survey Questions
fields.howto_description: Seven steps to write learning and development survey questions for the moment you ask them, build the survey, and act on the answers.
fields.howto_step_3_title: 03 Match questions to the four levels
fields.howto_step_1_des: Name the decision the answers will feed, such as which skill gets next year's first workshop or whether a program runs again. Put it in the first line of your prompt. Drop any question that would not change that decision.
fields.howto_step_2_des: Ask about skills before a program starts, about what people learned on the day it ends, and about what they do differently 60 to 90 days later. Give each moment its own short survey instead of one long survey at the end.
fields.howto_step_3_des: The Kirkpatrick model breaks evaluation into four levels. Reaction asks whether people found the training engaging, learning whether they acquired the intended knowledge and skills, and behavior whether they perform the new behaviors at work. Write at least one question per level.
fields.howto_step_4_des: Tell Emergent the program, who answers, the questions for each stage, and who reads the results. Emergent turns that description into the survey and a results dashboard. Change any question later by asking for it in one more sentence.
fields.howto_step_5_des: For the follow-up question, write a matching version for each learner's manager, worded about the learner. Asking both sides the same question shows whether a new habit is visible to someone else, not only to the person who took the course.
fields.howto_step_6_des: Send the link to 5 people from the group before launch and have them answer on a phone. Fix any question they read two ways, any rating scale without labels at both ends, and any skill name they never use at work.
fields.howto_step_7_des: When the survey closes, pick the lowest score and decide one change. Tell the group in a short note what the answers showed and what happens next. Send that note before the next survey goes out, not after it.

faq_plan.q: What are learning and development survey questions?
faq_plan.a: Learning and development survey questions ask employees about the skills they have, the training they took, and the growth they want next. Teams send them before a program to find gaps, right after it to check what people learned, and months later to see what changed at work.

faq_plan.q: How do I create learning and development survey questions?
faq_plan.a: Write a plain-English prompt that names the program, the stage, and who answers. Emergent's AI survey builder builds the survey from it, with a table for the answers and a dashboard for the scores. Share the link, then reword any question later with one more prompt.

faq_plan.q: Which learning and development survey questions come before a program?
faq_plan.a: Ask each person to rate their confidence in the skills their role needs, on a 1 to 5 scale. Then ask which skill would help most in the next 6 months and how they like to learn it, such as a workshop or a mentor. Keep it under 10 questions, short enough to finish on a break.

faq_plan.q: Can learning and development survey questions be light or playful?
faq_plan.a: One light opener is fine, such as asking which skill people would pick up if time were free. Keep the rest plain, because the answers feed budget decisions. For a team social or an icebreaker with no training decision behind it, a set of funny survey questions fits better.

faq_plan.q: When should learning and development survey questions go out after training?
faq_plan.a: Send reaction and knowledge questions within a day of the session, while the details are fresh. Wait 60 to 90 days for behavior questions, until people have had time to use the skill at work. Emergent builds both surveys from one prompt and keeps their answers in a database you own.

faq_plan.q: Should answers to learning and development survey questions be anonymous?
faq_plan.a: Make skill ratings and feedback on trainers anonymous, so a low self-rating carries no risk for the person who gives it. Keep names on knowledge checks and career goals, where the follow-up is personal. Say which is which in the invitation, and in a team of fewer than 5, drop team labels.

faq_plan.q: What rating scale fits learning and development survey questions?
faq_plan.a: Use one 5-point scale for every rating, labeled at both ends, such as 1 for not confident and 5 for very confident. The same scale lets this year's scores sit beside last year's. Factual items, like whether someone finished a course, read better as yes or no, and a yes no questions survey shows how to write them.

faq_plan.q: Which learning and development survey questions should managers answer?
faq_plan.a: Ask managers the same behavior question their team member gets, worded about that person: does this person now run weekly one-on-ones? Add which skill they want the team to build next and whether they had time to coach practice after the training. Emergent puts no response cap on the survey, and every manager can answer.

faq_plan.q: How do learning and development survey questions show whether training worked?
faq_plan.a: Ask the same skill ratings before the program and again 90 days after it, and test knowledge on the day it ends. When scores rise and managers confirm the new behavior, the training changed something for that group. When they stay flat, the comments usually say why, in the learners' own words.

faq_plan.q: Which learning and development survey questions explain dropouts?
faq_plan.a: Ask one multiple-choice question with the reasons people give, such as no time during shifts, content too basic, or a schedule clash, plus an optional comment box. Send it within a week of the first missed session. If you sell courses to outside customers who end a paid plan, a cancellation survey is the closer fit.

plan.angle: The top 10 are long lists of training feedback and career development questions (SurveyMonkey, Paycor, AIHR, SmartSurvey), one analytics blog and a Reddit thread, and none says which question belongs at which point of a program. This page sorts learning and development survey questions by the moment they are asked and the decision they feed: a skills check before the training plan, a knowledge check right after a session, a 90-day follow-up that asks the learner and the manager the same question, and a career goals survey that sizes next year's cohorts. Each tab ends in a decision an L&D lead made from the answers, and the how-to maps questions to the four Kirkpatrick levels, sourced to Kirkpatrick Partners.
